Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

rather adverb

preferably, instead

also would rather, I’d rather, rather than, prefer, instead, or rather, prefer … to, preference, would you rather, rather than (more truly)

classical

Mart. 8.67.9: māne venī potius
Ter. Ad. 74–75
Cic. Tusc. 2.52: perpessus est omnia potius quam cōnsciōs indicāret (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 368

potius

adverb; “rather than” is potius quam, with the subjunctive when two actions are compared

rather, sooner, preferably

Other words

  • magis … quam — rather (than), more truly: which word fits better

    adverb, with quam for the other term · also used · classical · Liv. 21.58.8: magis obrutī quam tēctī; Verg. Ecl. 1.11: mīror magis

    Potius is rather by preference, what one would sooner do; magis is rather by degree, what is more true: magis obrutī quam tēctī, buried rather than sheltered. Lewis & Short s.v. amplius: magis, “more, in the comparison of quality, and sometimes of action”; potius, “rather, the choice between different objects or acts”.

  • mālō, mālle, māluī — would rather, prefer

    verb, irregular, with an infinitive; “rather than” is quam, conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 2.12.2: praesentem audīre mālō; Quint. 1.1.12: ā sermōne Graecō puerum incipere mālō; Traupman 364

    “I’d rather” is the verb itself: mālō; politely, mālim.

  • vel potius — or rather (correcting oneself)

    also used · classical · Quint. 12.10.29: paene nōn hūmānā vōce vel omnīnō nōn vōce potius; Cic. Brut. 332: propemodum, vel plānē potius (Lewis & Short)

    A sharper correction is immō (see “actually”).

  • praeferō, praeferre, praetulī, praelātum — prefer (one thing to another)

    verb, irregular: aliquid alicui praeferre, conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 63: pecūniam praeferre amīcitiae; Traupman 364; Traupman 68

    Lewis & Short: “to place before another in esteem, to prefer” (very frequent).

  • antepōnō, antepōnere, anteposuī, antepositum — prefer, put before

    verb, third conjugation: aliquid alicui antepōnere · also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 17: amīcitiam omnibus rēbus hūmānīs antepōnātis

Examples

  • praesentem audīre mālō

    I’d rather hear it from you in personCic. Att. 2.12.2

  • Hoc patrium est, potius cōnsuēfacere fīlium suā sponte rēctē facere quam aliēnō metū.

    That is a father’s part: to get a son used to doing right of his own accord, rather than from fear of someone else.Ter. Ad. 74–75

  • vel sōlī tamen dīcāmus potius quam omnīnō nōn dīcāmus

    let us speak even on our own, rather than not speak at allQuint. 10.7.25

  • ego vōs hortārī tantum possum, ut amīcitiam omnibus rēbus hūmānīs antepōnātis

    all I can do is urge you to put friendship before everything else in human lifeCic. Amic. 17

  • legere oportet potius quam quatere

    they should be picked rather than shaken downVarr. RR 1.55.1

  • nōn equidem invideō; mīror magis

    I don’t envy you; rather, I wonderVerg. Ecl. 1.11

  • prōcumberent hominēs tegminibus suīs magis obrutī quam tēctī

    men fell, buried rather than sheltered by their shieldsLiv. 21.58.8

  • nōnne māvīs sine perīculō tuae domī esse quam cum perīculō aliēnae?

    wouldn’t you rather be safe in your own house than in danger in someone else’s?Cic. Fam. 4.7.4

  • Praeferō vīnum austērum vīnō dulcī.

    I prefer dry wine to sweet wine.Traupman 68

See also actually, quite, more.
